mn63:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn63:2.1: Then while the venerable Māluṅkyaputta was alone in meditation the following thought arose in his mind:
mn63:2.2: ‘There are these fields of views undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside and avoided by him:
mn63:2.3: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” or “the world is finite” or “the world is infinite” or “the soul is the same as the body” or “the soul is one and the body another” or “after death a Tathāgata is” or “after death a Tathāgata is not” or “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:2.4: the Blessed One does not declare these to me.
mn63:2.5: And it is not to my preference and liking that he does not declare them to me.
mn63:2.6: So I shall go to the Blessed One and ask him the meaning of this.
mn63:2.8: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …
mn63:2.9: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:2.10: then I will live the life divine under the Blessed One;
mn63:2.11: but if the Blessed One does not declare to me:
mn63:2.12: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …
mn63:2.13: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:2.14: then I will abandon the training and revert to the lower life.’
mn63:3.1: Then when it was evening, the venerable Māluṅkyaputta rose from meditation, and went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the venerable Māluṅkyaputta said to the Blessed One:
mn63:3.2: ‘Venerable sir, while I was alone in meditation the following thought arose in my mind—
mn63:3.3: there are these fields of views undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside and avoided by him:
mn63:3.4: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …
mn63:3.5: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:3.6: the Blessed One does not declare these to me.
mn63:3.7: And it is not to my preference and liking that he does not declare them to me.
mn63:3.8: So I shall go to the Blessed One and ask him the meaning of this.
mn63:3.10: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …
mn63:3.11: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:3.12: then I will live the life divine under the Blessed One.
mn63:3.13: But if the Blessed One does not declare to me:
mn63:3.14: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …
mn63:3.15: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:3.16: then I will abandon the training and revert to the lower life.’
mn63:3.18: “the world is eternal”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is eternal”;
mn63:3.20: “the world is not eternal”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is not eternal”.
mn63:3.21: If the Blessed One does not know
mn63:3.22: either “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):
mn63:3.23: “I do not know, I do not see.”
mn63:3.25: “the world is finite”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is finite”;
mn63:3.27: “the world is infinite”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is infinite”.
mn63:3.28: If the Blessed One does not know
mn63:3.29: either “the world is finite” or “the world is infinite”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):
mn63:3.30: “I do not know, I do not see.”
mn63:3.32: “the soul is the same as the body”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the soul is the same as the body”;
mn63:3.34: “the soul is one and the body another”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the soul is one and the body another”.
mn63:3.35: If the Blessed One does not know
mn63:3.36: either “the soul is the same as the body” or “the soul is one and the body another”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):
mn63:3.37: “I do not know, I do not see.”
mn63:3.39: “after death a Tathāgata is”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata is”;
mn63:3.41: “after death a Tathāgata is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata is not”.
mn63:3.42: If the Blessed One does not know
mn63:3.43: either “after death a Tathāgata is” or “after death a Tathāgata is not”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):
mn63:3.44: “I do not know, I do not see.”
mn63:3.46: “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”;
mn63:3.48: “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”.
mn63:3.49: If the Blessed One does not know
mn63:3.50: either “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):
mn63:3.51: “I do not know, I do not see.”’
mn63:4.1: ‘How then, Māluṅkyaputta, did I ever say to you:
mn63:4.2: “Come, Māluṅkyaputta, live the life divine under me and I will declare to you:
mn63:4.3: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ or ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’ or ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one and the body another’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”?’
mn63:4.6: “Venerable sir, I will live the life divine under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me:
mn63:4.7: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ or ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’ or ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one and the body another’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”?’
mn63:4.9: ‘So then, Māluṅkyaputta, I did not say to you:
mn63:4.10: “Come, Māluṅkyaputta, live the life divine under me and I will declare to you:
mn63:4.11: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …
mn63:4.12: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”;
mn63:4.13: nor did you say to me:
mn63:4.14: “Venerable sir, I will live the life divine under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me:
mn63:4.15: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …
mn63:4.16: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”.
mn63:4.17: That being so, misguided man, what are you and what are you forsaking?
mn63:5.2: “I will not live the life divine under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me:
mn63:5.3: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …
mn63:5.4: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”,
mn63:5.5: that would still remain undeclared by the Tathāgata and meanwhile that person would die.
mn63:5.6: Suppose, Māluṅkyaputta, a man were wounded by an arrow thickly smeared with poison,
mn63:5.7: and his friends and companions, his relatives and kin brought a surgeon to treat him.
mn63:5.9: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the man who wounded me, whether he is a warrior-noble or a brahmin or a merchant or a worker”;
mn63:5.11: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the name and clan of the man who wounded me”;
mn63:5.13: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me is tall or short or of middle height”;
mn63:5.15: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me is dark or brown or golden-skinned”;
mn63:5.17: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me lives in such a village or town or city”;
mn63:5.19: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the bow that wounded me, whether it was a long bow or a crossbow”;
mn63:5.21: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the bowstring that wounded me, whether it was made of swallow-wort fibre, or reed, or sinew, or hemp, or bark”;[^1]
mn63:5.23: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the shaft that wounded me, whether it was wild or cultivated”;
mn63:5.25: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know with whose feathers the shaft that wounded me was feathered, whether a vulture’s, or a crow’s, or a hawk’s, or a peacock’s, or a stork’s”;[^2]
mn63:5.27: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know with whose sinew the shaft that wounded me was bound, whether an ox’s, or a buffalo’s, or a lion’s, or a monkey’s”;[^3]
mn63:5.29: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the arrowhead that wounded me, whether it was hoof-tipped, or curved, or barbed, or calf-toothed, or shaped like an oleander leaf”—[^4]
mn63:5.30: that would still not be known to that man and meanwhile he would die.
mn63:5.31: So too, Māluṅkyaputta, if anyone should say thus:
mn63:5.32: “I will not live the life divine under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me:
mn63:5.33: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …
mn63:5.34: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”—
mn63:5.35: that would still remain undeclared by the Tathāgata and meanwhile that person would die.
mn63:6.1: ‘Māluṅkyaputta, there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is eternal”.
mn63:6.2: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is not eternal”.
mn63:6.3: And while there is the view “the world is eternal” or the view “the world is not eternal”, there is still birth, there is ageing, there is death, there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair,
mn63:6.4: of which I declare the destruction here and now.
mn63:6.5: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is finite”.
mn63:6.6: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is infinite”.
mn63:6.7: And while there is the view “the world is finite” or the view “the world is infinite”, there is still birth, there is ageing, there is death, there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair,
mn63:6.8: of which I declare the destruction here and now.
mn63:6.9: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “the soul is the same as the body”.
mn63:6.10: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the soul is one and the body another”.
mn63:6.11: And while there is the view “the soul is the same as the body” or the view “the soul is one and the body another”, there is still birth …
mn63:6.12: … of which I declare the destruction.
mn63:6.13: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is”.
mn63:6.14: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is not”.
mn63:6.15: And while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is” or the view “after death a Tathāgata is not”, there is still birth …
mn63:6.16: … of which I declare the destruction here and now.
mn63:6.17: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”.
mn63:6.18: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”.
mn63:6.19: And while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, there is still birth …
mn63:6.20: … of which I declare the destruction here and now.
mn63:7.1: ‘Consequently, Māluṅkyaputta, remember what is undeclared by me as undeclared,
mn63:7.2: and remember what is declared by me as declared.
mn63:7.3: And what is undeclared by me?
mn63:7.4: “The world is eternal” is undeclared by me;
mn63:7.11: “the soul is the same as the body”—
mn63:7.13: “the soul is one and the body another”—
mn63:7.19: “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”—
mn63:7.21: “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—
mn63:8.1: ‘And why is that undeclared by me?
mn63:8.2: It is because it is unconnected with the goal, it does not belong to the fundamentals of the life divine, it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.[^5]
mn63:8.3: That is why it is undeclared by me.
mn63:9.2: “This is suffering” is declared by me;
mn63:9.7: “this is the way leading to the cessation of suffering”—
mn63:10.1: ‘And why is that declared by me?
mn63:10.2: It is because it is connected with the goal, it belongs to the fundamentals of the life divine, and it leads to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn63:10.3: That is why it is declared by me.
mn63:10.4: ‘Consequently, Māluṅkyaputta, remember what is undeclared by me as undeclared,
mn63:10.5: and remember what is declared by me as declared.’
mn63:10.6: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn63:10.7: The venerable Māluṅkyaputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
